argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0304d: meeting "d" (detailed design) of series SY0304.

PROJECT
The team is designing a campus parking availability display.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Marketing Expert (ME)  Priya  present
B  User Interface designer (UI)  Tom  ABSENT, never speaks
C  Project Manager (PM)  Hannah  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Marcus  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0304a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, noted that the industrial designer was absent at a supplier visit, and had the team introduce themselves. She presented the brief from the university estates office: a parking availability display at each car park entrance showing free spaces, with an optional central sign near the main gate, a budget of about four hundred pounds per unit, and installation by the start of next term. The marketing expert described the main user problem as drivers circling for spaces, and the team agreed that the target users are staff, students and visitors, and that the display should show the number of free spaces with a colour-coded background. The marketing expert stated that the signs would be solar powered, but nobody agreed and the point was left unresolved. The project manager assigned the absent industrial designer to research sensing options and outdoor casing, and the team agreed to limit the scope to physical signs for now, with an app flagged as a possible later idea.
  decisions: The target users are staff, students and visitors. The display will show the number of free spaces with a green, amber or red colour behind it. The scope is limited to physical signs for now. An app is flagged as a possible later idea.
  actions: The industrial designer (absent) is to compare barrier counters and per-bay sensors with rough per-unit costs, and to look at whether the casing can survive outdoors. The project manager assigned this. The project manager will email the industrial designer about his task and send the minutes and the brief to the team. The marketing expert will survey about twenty to thirty campus users, students and staff, and try to include a few visitors. The user interface designer will sketch several screen layouts showing the number with a colour background, in a couple of screen sizes.
  problems: The power source is unresolved. Solar power was put forward as settled, but nobody agreed, and the user interface designer started to raise a concern about the underground car parks under the library. The sensing method is undecided: barrier counters are cheaper but may drift when cars tailgate. This is waiting on the industrial designer's research. Screen size is unknown and depends on the industrial designer. The budget of four hundred pounds per unit is tight for an outdoor screen. It is undecided whether the central sign near the main gate will be included.
  action item SY0304a.ai1: Research sensing options (barrier counters vs per-bay sensors) with rough per-unit costs, and check whether the casing can survive outdoor conditions, for the next meeting (owner D, active)
  action item SY0304a.ai2: Email the industrial designer about his assigned task and send the minutes and brief to the team (owner C, active)
  action item SY0304a.ai3: Survey about twenty to thirty campus users (students and staff, plus a few visitors) on what they want from the sign (owner A, active)
  action item SY0304a.ai4: Sketch several screen layouts combining the free-space number with a colour background, in a couple of screen sizes (owner B, active)
  fact (absence): Marcus, the industrial designer (D), was absent from the kickoff meeting because he was at a supplier visit for another project.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert stated that the signs would be solar powered and called it decided, but nobody agreed. The user interface designer began to raise a concern about the car parks under the library, and the project manager moved on without settling it.

[SY0304b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting with all four members present. She welcomed the industrial designer, who had missed the kickoff, and confirmed she had emailed him the brief and minutes. The marketing expert reported survey results from twenty-four people (fourteen students, eight staff, two visitors). Users want to read the number from the road before turning in, liked the colour coding, did not want adverts, and often asked for an app, which remains a later idea. The industrial designer compared barrier counters (about seventy pounds per entrance, but prone to drift from tailgating) with per-bay sensors (about thirty pounds per bay, over five thousand pounds for the library car park). He also recommended an IP65 outdoor casing and an LED number panel instead of an LCD screen. The user interface designer presented three layouts in two sizes. The team chose the larger sixty-centimetre LED display with the car park name on top and agreed the colour thresholds. They settled power on mains from the barrier supply, because the underground library car parks get no sun, and chose barrier counters with a nightly reset. This made the per-bay sensor quote the project manager had requested earlier in the meeting unnecessary, so it was cancelled. The estimated cost per sign is around four hundred pounds. The central sign near the main gate is still undecided pending input from the estates office.
  decisions: The display will be the larger size, about sixty centimetres wide. The number will be shown on an LED number panel rather than an LCD screen. The car park name will appear on top of the number. Colour thresholds: green above twenty free spaces, amber at twenty or fewer, red at five or fewer. The signs will run on mains power taken from the existing barrier supply, not solar. Sensing will use barrier counters with a nightly reset, and the attendant can enter a correction.
  actions: The industrial designer will check the mains connection at each barrier with the estates office and specify the casing properly. The user interface designer will produce the final layout at sixty centimetres, LED, with the car park name on top and the agreed colour thresholds. The marketing expert will survey more visitors at the main gate during next week's open day. The project manager will ask the estates office whether they want the central sign near the main gate and whether there is separate budget for it. The project manager will send the minutes round.
  problems: Making the number flash below ten free spaces was stated as settled by the user interface designer, but nobody agreed and the point was left unresolved. The estimated cost of about four hundred pounds per sign leaves no margin in the budget. Barrier counters can still drift during the day because of tailgating, which the nightly reset only partly addresses. It is undecided whether the central sign near the main gate will be included. It would need data from every car park via cabling or a wireless link. Visitors are under-represented in the survey, with only two respondents. Many users asked for an app, which remains out of scope for now.
  action item SY0304b.ai1: Get a proper quote from the supplier for per-bay sensors for the library car park (owner D, dropped)
  action item SY0304b.ai2: Check the mains connection at each barrier with the estates office and specify the outdoor casing properly (owner D, active)
  action item SY0304b.ai3: Produce the final layout at sixty centimetres, LED, with the car park name on top and the agreed colour thresholds (owner B, active)
  action item SY0304b.ai4: Survey more visitors by standing at the main gate during next week's open day (owner A, active)
  action item SY0304b.ai5: Ask the estates office whether they want the central sign near the main gate and whether there is separate budget for it (owner C, active)
  action item SY0304b.ai6: Send the minutes round to the team (owner C, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer stated that the number would flash below ten free spaces and called it settled, but nobody agreed. The industrial designer began to object and the project manager moved on to power.
  fact (action_item_removed): The per-bay sensor quote was cancelled by the project manager after the team chose barrier counters.

[SY0304c, conceptual design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the conceptual design meeting, noted that the industrial designer was off sick, and confirmed she had sent round the minutes of the previous meeting. She reported that the estates office would like the central sign near the main gate but has no separate budget for it, so the team left it out of this phase as a later idea. The user interface designer presented the sixty-centimetre layout with the car park name in white on a navy strip, the LED number below on a colour panel, and the agreed thresholds. The marketing expert reported that eleven visitors surveyed at the open day did not know the car park names and wanted a P symbol, and that most disliked flashing, which estates also discourage next to roads. The team therefore dropped flashing and cancelled the flashing mock-up. Relaying the industrial designer's email, the project manager reported that four of the five barriers have a spare mains supply but the underground library car park does not. She assigned the absent industrial designer to get an electrician's quote for a new supply there and to specify the mounting. The team chose a navy IP65 powder-coated aluminium casing and noted a cost of about three hundred and ninety pounds per sign, excluding the library supply.
  decisions: The central sign near the main gate is left out of this phase and flagged as a later idea. A P symbol will be added to the left of the car park name strip. The number will not flash. Red at five or fewer free spaces is the warning. The whole casing will be navy, matching the university signage. The barrier counters keep the nightly reset with attendant correction for now.
  actions: The industrial designer (absent) is to get an electrician's quote for running a new mains supply at the library car park and to specify the mounting (post or wall bracket), checking the wall mounting with estates. The project manager assigned this. The project manager will email the industrial designer to tell him about his task. The project manager will ask the estates office whether they could pay for the library electrics separately. The user interface designer will produce the final layout with the P symbol, the navy strip and no flashing, shown on the navy casing. The marketing expert will write up the open day survey results and send them round. The project manager will send the minutes round.
  problems: There is no spare mains supply at the underground library car park, and the cost of a new supply is unknown. It could push that sign over the four-hundred-pound budget. At about three hundred and ninety pounds per sign, only about ten pounds of margin is left. Barrier counter drift is still only partly addressed by the nightly reset. The marketing expert's suggestion of a QR code on the casing for a future app was not agreed and was left open. The visitor survey sample is still small, with eleven open day visitors plus two earlier respondents.
  action item SY0304c.ai1: Make an animated mock-up of the layout with and without flashing so the team can compare them (owner B, dropped)
  action item SY0304c.ai2: Get an electrician's quote for running a new mains supply at the library car park, and specify the mounting (post or wall bracket), checking the wall mounting with estates (owner D, active)
  action item SY0304c.ai3: Email the industrial designer to tell him about the electrician quote and mounting task (owner C, active)
  action item SY0304c.ai4: Ask the estates office whether they could pay for the library car park electrics separately (owner C, active)
  action item SY0304c.ai5: Produce the final layout with the P symbol, the navy strip and no flashing, shown on the navy casing (owner B, active)
  action item SY0304c.ai6: Write up the open day survey results and send them round (owner A, active)
  action item SY0304c.ai7: Send the minutes round to the team (owner C, active)
  fact (absence): Marcus, the industrial designer (D), was absent from the conceptual design meeting because he was off sick.
  fact (action_item_removed): The project manager cancelled the flashing mock-up after the team decided against flashing.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert proposed a QR code on the casing for a future app. The user interface designer doubted it, and the project manager deferred it without agreement.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F3_UNAGREED_DECISION [F3]: Someone raises a proposal as if it were a decision, but no one agrees to it and the meeting moves on without settling it. Record an F3 fact of type unagreed_proposal with agreed false. It must not appear in summary.decisions.
  Required gold labels: summary, qa_facts, edge_cases.
- F3_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F3]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. Record F3 facts for who was absent, who got the task, and who assigned it, so a later question ("what was X asked to do while they were away?") can be answered.
  Required gold labels: action_items, qa_facts, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
